title.rendered: AfDB invests US$15M in Biovac to advance African vaccine manufacturing sovereignty

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SOUTH AFRICA—The African Development Bank Group (AfDB) has finalised a loan of up to US$15 million to the Biologicals and Vaccines Institute of South Africa (Biovac) to support the construction of a multi-vaccine manufacturing facility in Cape Town.

The project is expected to significantly increase Africa’s capacity to produce vaccines locally and reduce reliance on imports.

The financing forms part of Biovac’s expansion programme, which aims to increase the company’s annual manufacturing capacity to as many as 500 million vaccine doses.

Once completed, the facility is expected to make Biovac Africa’s first end-to-end producer of oral cholera vaccines and South Africa’s first local manufacturer of inactivated polio vaccines (IPV).

The project will also enable Biovac to produce IPV through technology-transfer partnerships with Sanofi, the International Vaccine Institute, Biological E Limited, EuBiologics and Bharat Biotech.

For more than two decades, Biovac has served as South Africa’s primary vaccine supplier.

Strengthening Africa’s vaccine manufacturing capacity

Africa currently imports more than 99% of the vaccines it uses, despite carrying a disproportionate share of the global burden of vaccine-preventable diseases.

To address this gap, the African Union has set a target of producing 60% of the continent’s vaccines locally by 2040.

In addition to expanding vaccine production, the Biovac project is expected to create approximately 340 full-time jobs.

About 43% of these positions are projected to go to women, while 30% will be allocated to young people.

Biovac, which already employs more than 300 people, about half of whom are women, will also expand training programmes in vaccine manufacturing, quality control and regulatory science.

The programmes will be delivered in partnership with local universities and other regional training institutions.

“This investment in Biovac is about much more than expanding vaccine production capacity. It is about building Africa’s health sovereignty, strengthening regional value chains, and creating industrial capabilities that will enable the continent to respond more effectively to future health emergencies,” said Solomon Quaynor, AfDB Vice President for Private Sector, Infrastructure and Industrialisation.

Facility to produce vaccines for major diseases

The new facility is expected to be completed by 2028.

It will initially manufacture oral cholera vaccines before expanding into IPV, pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) and MenX vaccines for meningitis.

The project is also designed to benefit from Africa’s emerging vaccine-financing mechanisms, including Gavi’s African Vaccine Manufacturing Accelerator (AVMA).

The US$1.2 billion mechanism provides milestone payments to African vaccine manufacturers that achieve World Health Organization prequalification, as well as per-dose financial support for vaccines supplied through UNICEF tenders.

The AfDB is joining a group of development finance institutions supporting the project.

The syndicate is led by the International Finance Corporation and includes a long-term quasi-equity facility from the Human Development Accelerator programme, a European Union-backed initiative implemented by the European Investment Bank in partnership with the Gates Foundation.

The financing package will also receive grant funding and technical support from global health partners to facilitate technology transfers and expand Biovac’s vaccine portfolio.

“We welcome the African Development Bank as a partner in this landmark project,” said Biovac Chief Executive Officer Morena Makhoana.

“The project will shift the narrative from majority-imported vaccines to majority-exported vaccines.”

Established in 2003 through a partnership between Biovac and the South African government, Biovac is a Cape Town-based biopharmaceutical company focused on developing local vaccine manufacturing capacity.

It currently manufactures and supplies routine paediatric vaccines and has delivered more than 450 million vaccine doses across Southern Africa, including COVID-19 vaccines.

title.rendered: Samsung Biologics to acquire PolyPeptide Group for US$1.8B to expand peptide drug manufacturing

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SOUTH KOREA—Samsung Biologics has announced an all-cash public tender offer to acquire Switzerland-based PolyPeptide Group for CHF1.46 billion (US$1.8 billion), marking the largest biopharmaceutical merger and acquisition in South Korea’s history.

The proposed acquisition reflects Samsung Biologics’ strategy to broaden its contract development and manufacturing capabilities by expanding into peptide-based active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), a rapidly growing segment of the pharmaceutical industry.

Under the terms of the offer, PolyPeptide shareholders will receive CHF44.31 (US$54.60) per share in cash.

Subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals, Samsung Biologics expects to complete the transaction before the end of the year.

Strategic expansion into peptide therapeutics

Samsung Biologics is pursuing the acquisition as demand for peptide therapeutics continues to accelerate, particularly amid the global success of GLP-1 medicines for treating obesity and type 2 diabetes.

By adding peptide manufacturing capabilities to its portfolio, the company aims to strengthen its position as a comprehensive contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO).

Peptide therapeutics are medicines made from short chains of amino acids. Several of the latest obesity and diabetes treatments belong to this class of drugs, including GLP-1 receptor agonists, which help regulate blood sugar levels while reducing appetite.

As pharmaceutical companies continue to invest heavily in these therapies, manufacturers with peptide production expertise have become increasingly valuable.

Samsung Biologics said the acquisition will complement its established strengths in antibody therapeutics and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs).

At the same time, it will enable the company to meet growing customer demand for a wider range of biologic drug manufacturing services across multiple therapeutic modalities.

PolyPeptide strengthens Samsung’s global manufacturing network

The acquisition will also significantly expand Samsung Biologics’ international footprint.

PolyPeptide operates research, development and commercial manufacturing facilities across Sweden, Belgium, France, the United States and India, providing Samsung with an established global production network and specialized peptide expertise.

Headquartered in Baar, Switzerland, PolyPeptide Group traces its origins to a business that was spun off from pharmaceutical company Ferring in 1996.

Since then, the company has developed and manufactured more than 1,000 therapeutic peptides for customers worldwide, establishing itself as a leading specialist in peptide-based APIs.

Peter Wilden, chairman of PolyPeptide, said the board unanimously supports the proposed transaction after evaluating its strategic alternatives.

“After a comprehensive review of strategic options, the Board is convinced that Samsung Biologics’ offer is compelling for our shareholders, delivering an attractive cash price and immediate, certain value today,” Wilden said.

Meanwhile, investors responded cautiously to the announcement, with Samsung Biologics shares falling 1.3% in early Monday trading despite the proposed acquisition’s strategic significance.

title.rendered: UNICEF, Gavi launch global push to accelerate Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine development

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]

USA—UNICEF and Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, have launched a global call for information from vaccine developers and manufacturers to accelerate the development and availability of vaccines against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.

The initiative follows Gavi’s commitment of up to US$40 million to accelerate access to potential vaccines by supporting manufacturing scale-up and ensuring that doses can be produced rapidly if clinical trials demonstrate safety and effectiveness.

The funding forms part of a broader US$50 million package released through Gavi’s First Response Fund to support both outbreak response activities and vaccine development.

Gathering critical information from developers

Through the newly announced request for expressions of interest, UNICEF and Gavi are seeking detailed information on vaccine candidates, development timelines, manufacturing capacity, regulatory plans, and production readiness.

The information will help partners prioritize the most promising candidates and identify pathways for accelerating access should an effective vaccine emerge.

The effort is being coordinated with key global health partners, including the World Health Organization (WHO), the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), and UNICEF.

Gavi has indicated that proposals involving vaccine production in Africa will receive particular consideration as part of broader efforts to strengthen regional manufacturing capacity.

Several vaccine candidates advance

Currently, no vaccine has been approved specifically for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola.

However, several candidates are advancing through preclinical and early clinical development.

Among the leading contenders is an rVSV-based vaccine being developed by the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative (IAVI).

The organization has confirmed that it is working closely with UNICEF and Gavi and expects to transfer vaccine materials to a manufacturing partner in the coming weeks.

Human clinical trials could begin before the end of 2026 if development proceeds as planned.

Other candidates include the ChAdOx1 vaccine, developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, as well as an mRNA-based vaccine from Moderna, supported by CEPI.

Earlier this month, CEPI announced approximately US$60 million in funding to accelerate the development of Bundibugyo Ebola vaccine candidates, with Moderna receiving up to US$50 million for preclinical studies and early-stage clinical trials.

In addition, Public Health Vaccines is developing a vaccine based on technology similar to that used in Merck’s Ebola vaccine, Ervebo, which is approved for the Zaire strain of the virus but not for Bundibugyo Ebola.

Growing Outbreak Drives Urgency

The push for vaccine development comes as the ongoing outbreak continues to expand across affected regions.

More than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths have been reported in the DRC and Uganda, making it one of the most significant Bundibugyo Ebola outbreaks on record.

Health authorities have warned that the absence of an approved vaccine leaves communities vulnerable and underscores the need for rapid investment in research, manufacturing, and emergency preparedness.

To support these efforts, Gavi is using its First Response Fund to finance manufacturing readiness, facilitate regulatory pathways, and secure early access to investigational vaccine doses for emergency deployment.

The organization says early investment is essential to ensure that vaccine manufacturers can move quickly from successful clinical trials to large-scale production when needed.

title.rendered: CinnaGen secures historic European approval for osteoporosis biosimilar Zandoriah

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||41px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

UK—CinnaGen has secured a major regulatory milestone after the European Commission granted centralised marketing authorisation for Zandoriah® (teriparatide), a biosimilar to Eli Lilly’s Forsteo®, for the treatment of osteoporosis in adults.

The approval allows the company to market the medicine across all 27 European Union member states, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway, subject to national pricing, reimbursement, and market-access requirements.

The decision marks CinnaGen’s first-ever marketing authorisation within the European Union and represents a significant step in the Iranian biopharmaceutical company’s expansion into highly regulated international markets.

The approval follows a positive opinion issued in February by the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP), which concluded that Zandoriah demonstrated comparable quality, safety, and efficacy to the reference product.

Addressing a growing osteoporosis burden

Zandoriah enters a market where osteoporosis continues to place a substantial burden on patients and healthcare systems.

According to industry data, the disease was linked to approximately 4.3 million fragility fractures across the EU 27, the United Kingdom, and Switzerland in 2019.

These fractures generated healthcare costs exceeding €56 billion (US$64.4 billion) annually, while an estimated 71% of women eligible for osteoporosis treatment remained untreated.

The newly approved biosimilar contains teriparatide, a recombinant form of parathyroid hormone used to stimulate bone formation and reduce fracture risk in patients with osteoporosis.

 It is indicated for postmenopausal women, men at increased risk of fractures, and patients whose osteoporosis is associated with long-term glucocorticoid therapy.

Expanding access through biosimilars

CinnaGen believes the introduction of another EU-authorised teriparatide biosimilar could help improve patient access while supporting the sustainability of healthcare systems through increased competition.

With the approval in place, the company plans to work with its commercial and distribution partners on country-specific launch strategies, market-access activities, supply planning, pharmacovigilance alignment, and participation in public tenders across Europe.

The company said its biosimilar programme is supported by integrated manufacturing capabilities, regulatory expertise, and quality systems designed to meet international standards.

A landmark achievement for CinnaGen

Dr. Haleh Hamedifar, Chairperson of CinnaGen Group, described the authorisation as the result of years of investment in scientific expertise, manufacturing excellence, quality systems, and regulatory compliance.

Chief Executive Officer Mehran Montajabi Niyat said the approval provides partners with an EU-authorized biosimilar around which they can build long-term launch and supply strategies.

The approval has also attracted attention within the pharmaceutical industry, as it marks the first medicine from CinnaGen to receive European Union marketing authorisation.

Industry observers have described the achievement as a landmark moment for the company, which previously obtained EU Good Manufacturing Practice certification and has marketed teriparatide in Iran for more than a decade under the brand name Cinopar.

According to Fierce Pharma, country-level launch dates, reimbursement decisions, and product availability will vary across European markets depending on local regulatory and commercial arrangements.

title.rendered: Zydus Lifesciences to acquire Assertio Holdings in US$166.4M deal to expand US oncology portfolio

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||14px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

USA—Zydus Lifesciences has agreed to acquire all outstanding common shares of Assertio Holdings in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately US$166.4 million.

The acquisition will be carried out through Zydus Worldwide DMCC, a subsidiary of Zydus, and marks another major step in the company’s efforts to strengthen its specialty pharmaceutical business in the United States.

Under the agreement, Zydus will acquire Assertio shares at US$23.50 per share in cash.

The offer represents a 30.6% premium over Garda Therapeutics’ earlier US$18.00 per share bid announced on 8 April 2026 and a 7.8% premium over Garda’s revised US$21.80 per share offer made on 4 May 2026.

Assertio’s Board of Directors determined that the Zydus proposal constituted a “superior proposal” under the terms of the revised Garda merger agreement.

Focus on Oncology and specialty therapies

The acquisition will give Zydus access to Assertio’s commercial infrastructure in the US specialty pharmaceutical market, particularly in oncology supportive care and pain management therapies.

Assertio’s portfolio includes Rolvedon (eflapegrastim-xnst), a long-acting granulocyte colony-stimulating factor biologic approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for the prevention of febrile neutropenia in adult cancer patients undergoing myelosuppressive chemotherapy.

Assertio’s board also highlighted the certainty attached to the Zydus proposal, noting that the transaction carries no financing contingency and is fully guaranteed by a financially strong Zydus entity.

The structure gives Assertio direct recourse in the event of a breach or failure to close the transaction.

Heather Mason, chairperson of Assertio’s board, said the company conducted a comprehensive strategic review before approving the deal.

She added that the board carefully assessed the transaction’s value, execution certainty, and overall terms before concluding that the Zydus offer represented the best available option for shareholders.

Tender offer and delisting plans

Zydus will shortly begin a tender offer to acquire all outstanding Assertio shares.

The transaction is expected to close during the second quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including the tender of a majority of Assertio’s shares.

Once the tender process concludes, Zydus plans to acquire any remaining shares through a second-step merger at the same price of US$23.50 per share.

Following completion, Assertio’s common stock will be delisted from Nasdaq.

Moelis & Company is serving as financial adviser to Assertio, while Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher is acting as legal counsel.

Longacre Square Partners is advising on strategy and communications.

Zydus expands global specialty business

The Assertio acquisition continues Zydus’ broader expansion into specialty and high-value pharmaceutical markets globally.

In December 2025, the company signed an exclusive licensing and supply agreement with Formycon for FYB206, a biosimilar version of MSD’s Keytruda (Pembrolizumab), covering the US and Canadian markets.

In separate developments announced this week, Zydus also revealed that its board will meet on 19 May 2026 to consider a share buyback proposal, a move that boosted investor sentiment and lifted the company’s shares by nearly 6% in trading.

title.rendered: Cipla South Africa to supply critical childhood vaccines in new state tender

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||14px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

SOUTH AFRICA—Cipla South Africa has secured a major public sector vaccine tender, reinforcing its role in supporting South Africa’s national immunisation programme through the supply of affordable, high-quality vaccines for children and vulnerable communities.

The award marks another milestone in the company’s long-standing partnership with the country’s public healthcare sector and expands its growing presence in the vaccine market.

The pharmaceutical company submitted bids across several critical childhood immunisation categories, including the Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine (PCV10), Rotavirus vaccine, and paediatric Hepatitis B vaccine.

These vaccines remain essential in preventing severe childhood illnesses such as pneumonia, diarrhoeal disease, meningitis, and hepatitis-related complications, which continue to place pressure on healthcare systems across the region.

Expanding support for national immunization goals

According to Paul Miller, CEO of Cipla Africa, the tender award reflects the company’s commitment to strengthening national immunisation priorities and improving access to preventative healthcare.

He explained that Cipla’s growing participation in multiple vaccine categories demonstrates its focus on addressing pressing public health challenges while improving health outcomes for children and communities.

Miller added that robust immunisation programmes remain one of the most effective ways to reduce preventable diseases, improve long-term public health, and narrow healthcare inequalities.

He noted that ensuring reliable vaccine availability and timely distribution remains critical to protecting vulnerable populations, particularly in underserved communities where access to healthcare services can still be inconsistent.

Cipla said its vaccine portfolio is supported by stringent quality standards and a strong emphasis on supply continuity, an area that has become increasingly important amid global concerns about medicine shortages and procurement disruptions.

Focus on local manufacturing and reliable supply

The latest vaccine tender award comes only months after Cipla reaffirmed its support for South Africa’s antiretroviral (ARV) supply programme following disruptions involving other suppliers in the country’s HIV treatment market.

Earlier this year, the company announced expanded local manufacturing capacity for ARV medicines, including increased tablet-filling capacity and investments to strengthen domestic pharmaceutical production.

Cipla has maintained a long-standing relationship with South Africa’s Department of Health through the supply of ARVs and vaccines under national healthcare programmes.

The company stated that its current focus remains on maintaining reliability, consistency, and responsible collaboration with the public sector.

In addition, Cipla South Africa continues to work with healthcare stakeholders on initiatives designed to improve vaccine awareness and reduce vaccine hesitancy.

The company said these efforts align with its broader healthcare mission of supporting preventative medicine and improving long-term public health sustainability through stronger immunisation coverage.

title.rendered: Merck completes US$6.7B acquisition of Terns Pharmaceuticals to strengthen the leukemia drug pipeline

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||14px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

USA—Merck & Co., known as MSD outside the United States and Canada, has completed its acquisition of Terns Pharmaceuticals in a transaction valued at approximately US$6.7 billion.

The move strengthens Merck’s hematology and oncology pipeline through the addition of TERN-701, an investigational therapy for chronic myeloid leukemia (CML), as the pharmaceutical giant continues to expand through science-focused acquisitions.

The acquisition follows Merck’s announcement in late March that it would acquire the California-based clinical-stage biotech company for US$53.00 per share, representing a significant premium over Terns’ recent average trading price.

The deal also came shortly after the expiration of the waiting period under the U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act, clearing a major regulatory hurdle ahead of closing.

Commenting on the acquisition, Merck chairman and chief executive officer Robert M. Davis said the transaction reflects the company’s continued commitment to science-driven, value-enhancing business development.

He noted that TERN-701 has the potential to become a differentiated treatment option for certain patients with chronic myeloid leukemia and said Merck looks forward to advancing its clinical development with the Terns team.

TERN-701 at the center of the deal

The acquisition centers on TERN-701, a novel oral allosteric BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor designed to target the ABL myristoyl pocket.

The investigational therapy recently received Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for the treatment of adults with Philadelphia chromosome-positive chronic-phase CML who lack the T315I mutation and have previously received two or more tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

The designation was based on encouraging data from the ongoing Phase 1/2 CARDINAL trial, which is evaluating the therapy’s safety and efficacy in patients with relapsed or resistant disease.

Industry analysts view the designation as a significant regulatory milestone that could accelerate TERN-701’s development timeline.

Transaction structure and financial impact

Merck completed the acquisition through a cash tender offer conducted by a subsidiary.

As of the offer’s expiration on May 4, 2026, approximately 100.1 million shares, representing 86.36% of Terns’ outstanding common stock, had been validly tendered.

Following the tender offer, Merck finalized the acquisition through a merger that converted all remaining outstanding shares into the right to receive US$53.00 in cash per share.

Terns has now become a wholly owned subsidiary of Merck, and its common stock has ceased trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

Merck said it expects to record a US$5.8 billion research and development charge, equivalent to about US$2.35 per share, in its second-quarter and full-year 2026 financial results.

The company also expects an additional earnings-per-share impact of approximately US$0.12 this year as it funds TERN-701’s continued clinical development and associated financing costs.

title.rendered: Egypt’s medical supplies sector pushes for procurement price reforms amid rising costs

content.rendered:
[et_pb_section fb_built=”1″ _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_row _builder_version=”4.27.5″ _module_preset=”default” custom_margin=”6px|auto||auto||” custom_padding=”15px|||14px||” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_column type=”4_4″ _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”][et_pb_text _builder_version=”4.27.4″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” theme_builder_area=”post_content”]

EGYPT—The medical supplies sector in Egypt is preparing to submit a memorandum to Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly, seeking urgent revisions to government procurement prices as production and supply costs continue to rise sharply.

This move comes as suppliers face mounting financial pressure driven by increased expenses for raw materials, transportation, and insurance.

In response, the Egyptian Authority for Unified Procurement has introduced a series of measures aimed at easing operational strain and maintaining a steady flow of essential medical supplies.

Amr Gad, Deputy Head of the authority for the medical supplies sector, confirmed that all purchase orders older than five weeks that remain unfulfilled will be cancelled and reissued.

This step is intended to reduce administrative and financial burdens on both manufacturers and traders.

Furthermore, the authority has committed to significantly shortening payment cycles.

Suppliers delivering goods for Egypt’s strategic stockpile will now receive payments within 30 to 45 days, compared to the previous 120-day period.

In addition, companies can now substitute bank guarantee letters with a portion of their outstanding dues, a move designed to ease liquidity challenges.

Suppliers seek price adjustments

At the same time, Mohamed Ismail Abdo, Head of the Medical Supplies Division at the Cairo Chamber of Commerce, emphasized that suppliers remain committed to meeting national demand and supporting the buildup of a strategic reserve.

However, he noted that companies are facing cost increases of at least 100% across several components, including logistics and raw materials, alongside the depreciation of the Egyptian pound.

To support the memorandum, division members have been asked to submit detailed data on deliveries made during March and April, including quantities and total values.

This data will help justify the sector’s request for price adjustments that better reflect current market conditions.

Abdo also urged companies to fulfill their supply commitments to the procurement authority, as well as to hospitals affiliated with the Ministry of Health and Population, public health insurance entities, and university hospitals before the end of April.

Concerns over market pricing practices

Meanwhile, the division has compiled invoices from private hospitals showing significant price disparities.

According to Abdo, some hospitals charge patients around EGP 1,200 (USD 24) for a box of medical gloves, while suppliers sell the same products at EGP 170–180 (USD 3.40–3.60).

Separately, Mari Gamal, Head of Central Administration at the procurement authority, has called on companies to provide updated data on inventory levels, including finished goods, raw materials, and monthly supply volumes.

She stressed that accurate data is essential for planning tenders and ensuring the completion of the country’s strategic medical supplies reserve.

Gamal also noted that the authority has already finalized Egypt’s pharmaceutical stockpile and has consistently avoided imposing delay penalties on suppliers to support the sector.

title.rendered: Arabian Ethicals champions pharmaceutical distribution at Sharjah’s ICPM 2026

UAE—Arabian Ethicals, a Ghobash Group enterprise, has participated in the International Conference on Pharmacy and Medicine (ICPM) held from January 20–22 in Sharjah.

The conference provided a crucial platform for addressing the evolving challenges and opportunities within the Middle East’s pharmaceutical and healthcare landscape.

Ebru Yavuz, General Manager of Arabian Ethicals, joined high-level discussions focusing on healthcare access, pharmaceutical innovation, and regulatory frameworks across the region.

Her participation underscored the company’s commitment to advancing healthcare delivery standards throughout the Middle East.

Bringing together key healthcare stakeholders

ICPM has established itself as a significant regional platform for the pharmaceutical and healthcare sector.

The conference attracted regulators, manufacturers, healthcare providers, and industry stakeholders who gathered to examine priorities shaping modern healthcare delivery.

This diverse representation created an environment conducive to meaningful dialogue about the sector’s most pressing concerns.

During the event, Yavuz shared valuable insights on how pharmaceutical distribution ensures safe, compliant, and uninterrupted access to medicines across the region.

Her expertise highlighted the often underappreciated yet vital role that distribution plays in maintaining healthcare system functionality.

Understanding distribution as healthcare infrastructure

Yavuz delivered a presentation titled “Powering Healthcare Access: The Middle East Distribution Imperative,” which positioned distribution as a central pillar of the healthcare ecosystem.

She drew extensively on the UAE market context to illustrate how distributors function as the operational and regulatory bridge connecting global manufacturers, health authorities, and healthcare providers.

“Distribution is foundational to healthcare access,” Yavuz explained.

“In the UAE, it is the mechanism that ensures medicines are properly authorized, managed in line with regulatory standards, and consistently available, while safeguarding quality and patient safety.”

Navigating Complex Regulatory Requirements

Yavuz emphasized that pharmaceutical products cannot be legally imported, stored, or sold without an authorized distributor.

She outlined the distributor’s responsibility to maintain alignment with federal and local regulatory requirements, including product registration, dossier compliance, and ongoing pharmacovigilance measures to protect public safety.

These regulatory functions extend beyond simple paperwork.

They represent a comprehensive system ensuring that every medication reaching patients meets stringent quality and safety standards established by UAE health authorities.

Maintaining supply chain integrity in challenging conditions

A significant portion of the discussion centered on supply chain integrity and Good Distribution Practice (GDP) compliance.

Yavuz addressed the importance of validated cold-chain infrastructure, temperature monitoring, serialization, and traceability in preserving product quality.

These measures become particularly critical in extreme climate conditions and for temperature-sensitive therapies such as biologics, vaccines, and insulin.

The UAE’s climate presents unique challenges that require specialized infrastructure and rigorous protocols to maintain medication efficacy throughout the distribution process.

Ensuring continuous access across the Emirates

Yavuz also discussed the distributor’s role in supporting market access and ensuring continuity of supply across the UAE.

This includes tender participation, demand planning, forecasting, and inventory management.

These functions prove critical to maintaining uninterrupted availability of essential and chronic medications across hospitals, pharmacies, and healthcare providers throughout all seven emirates.

Her contribution formed part of broader ICPM discussions examining how healthcare systems can balance innovation with regulatory rigor and operational resilience, reinforcing distribution as a foundational enabler of patient access.

Headquartered in Dubai, Arabian Ethicals works closely with international pharmaceutical partners to connect global innovation with local healthcare providers, ensuring compliant and reliable access to medicines across the UAE.
